extracted.intended_audience: external experts (Evaluators, Rapporteurs, Vice-Chairs) appointed to evaluate MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposals for Horizon Europe
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal evaluation rules for external experts assessing Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowship (MSCA-PF) proposals, covering Individual Evaluation Reports, Consensus Reports, scoring, evaluation criteria, conflicts of interest, and proposal format. Targeted at people performing remote evaluation in SEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Excellence (weight 50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: EXCELLENCE is about: quality and pertinence of the R&I objectives; soundness of the methodology; relevance of interdisciplinary approaches, gender and diversity aspects; quality of the planned open science practices; quality of the supervision; the researcher’s existing professional experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the proposal addresses research and innovation objectives, methodology, interdisciplinarity, gender/diversity where relevant, open science practices, supervision and researcher experience. Open science practices should be implemented as an integral part of the methodology and are evaluated under Excellence. If the proposal has appropriate justifications for not including open science practices, do not penalise it; if open science is not sufficiently addressed consider adding a shortcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-criterion 1.1: Quality and pertinence of the project's research and innovation objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: QUALITY AND PERTINENCE OF THE PROJECT’S RESEARCH AND INNOVATION OBJECTIVES (AND THE EXTENT TO WHICH THEY ARE AMBITIOUS, AND GO BEYOND THE STATE OF THE ART).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate quality and pertinence of objectives; extent to which proposed work is ambitious and goes beyond the state of the art; whether objectives are realistically achievable, measurable and verifiable. Use evidence from proposal; do not base judgements on potential changes or external sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-criterion 1.2: Soundness of the proposed methodology (including interdisciplinarity, gender/diversity, open science)
rubrics_metrics.description: SOUNDNESS OF THE PROPOSED METHODOLOGY (INCLUDING INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACHES, CONSIDERATION OF THE GENDER DIMENSION AND OTHER DIVERSITY ASPECTS IF RELEVANT FOR THE RESEARCH PROJECT, AND THE QUALITY OF OPEN SCIENCE PRACTICES).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess soundness of concepts, models and assumptions; identification of methodological challenges and proposed measures to tackle them; relevance and integration of interdisciplinary approaches; how gender and other diversity aspects are incorporated if relevant (or justified if not relevant). Specifically evaluate open science practices as part of methodology: Data Management Plan (DMP), Open Access to research data where possible, and any other open science practices explained. Do not evaluate Open Access to peer-reviewed publications (this is a contractual obligation). If open science is not appropriate, check justification; insufficient addressing may be a shortcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-criterion 1.3: Quality of the supervision, training and two-way transfer of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: QUALITY OF THE SUPERVISION, TRAINING AND OF THE TWO-WAY TRANSFER OF KNOWLEDGE BETWEEN THE RESEARCHER AND THE HOST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate supervisors' qualifications and experience in the research topic and in supervising postdoctoral researchers; supervisors' time, commitment and mechanisms for progress, review and feedback. Assess effectiveness of planned training (scientific, management/organisation, horizontal and key transferable skills). For European Fellowships assess two-way transfer of knowledge host↔researcher; for Global Fellowships assess three-way transfer (researcher, host, associated partner). If a non-academic placement is included, assess its rationale and added value under 1.3. Proposals without non-academic placements must not be penalised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-criterion 1.4: Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills
rubrics_metrics.description: QUALITY AND APPROPRIATENESS OF THE RESEARCHER’S PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE, COMPETENCES AND SKILLS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 1.4 take into account the CV and the researcher’s track-record relative to their level of experience. Assess whether the professional experience, competences and skills are appropriate for the proposed research. Consider eligibility requirements (doctoral degree obtained by call deadline; maximum 8 years full-time equivalent research experience unless justified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Impact (weight 30%)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPACT is about: the enhancement of the researcher’s career perspectives and skills development expected through the proposal implementation; dissemination, exploitation and communication of the research; direct scientific, societal and economic impact of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the proposal will enhance career prospects and skills, the plans for dissemination/exploitation/communication, and the direct impacts. Use sub-criteria 2.1–2.3 to structure comments. Ensure dissemination/exploitation/communication measures are concrete and proportionate to the project scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-criterion 2.1: Credibility of measures to enhance career perspectives and employability and skills development
rubrics_metrics.description: CREDIBILITY OF THE MEASURES TO ENHANCE THE CAREER PERSPECTIVES AND EMPLOYABILITY OF THE RESEARCHER AND CONTRIBUTION TO THEIR SKILLS DEVELOPMENT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate expected career perspectives inside and/or outside academia, expected skills development, and credibility of the planned measures to achieve these. Check realism and clarity of training and career-enhancing activities described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-criterion 2.2: Suitability and quality of measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts (dissemination, exploitation, communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: SUITABILITY AND QUALITY OF THE MEASURES TO MAXIMISE EXPECTED OUTCOMES AND IMPACTS, AS SET OUT IN THE DISSEMINATION AND EXPLOITATION PLAN, INCLUDING COMMUNICATION ACTIVITIES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess dissemination, exploitation and communication measures: whether they are concrete, appropriate to target groups, proportionate to the scale of the project, and whether intellectual property management/protection strategy is addressed when relevant. Evaluate planning of communication and public engagement activities (objectives, messages, tools and channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-criterion 2.3: Magnitude and importance of project's contribution to expected scientific, societal and economic impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: THE MAGNITUDE AND IMPORTANCE OF THE PROJECT’S CONTRIBUTION TO THE EXPECTED SCIENTIFIC, SOCIETAL AND ECONOMIC IMPACTS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magnitude: evaluate how widespread the outcomes/impacts are likely to be (size/proportion of target group benefiting over time). Importance: evaluate the value of those benefits (e.g., additional healthy life years, efficiency savings). Assess credibility of quantified estimates of impact and whether impacts extend beyond the immediate scope/duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Quality and Efficiency of the Implementation (weight 20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: QUALITY AND EFFICIENCY OF THE IMPLEMENTATION is about: quality and effectiveness of the work plan; risk assessment and contingency plan; quality and capacity of all participating organisations, including non-scientific hosting arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess work plan coherence, risk identification and mitigation, allocation of effort, and capacity of participating organisations and hosting arrangements. Consider infrastructure, logistics and support services. Check consistency between Gantt chart, work packages, deliverables, milestones, secondments and placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-criterion 3.1: Quality and effectiveness of the work plan, risk assessment and appropriateness of effort
rubrics_metrics.description: QUALITY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF THE WORK PLAN, ASSESSMENT OF RISKS AND APPROPRIATENESS OF THE EFFORT ASSIGNED TO WORK PACKAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate quality/effectiveness of the work plan (deliverables, milestones), appropriateness of effort assigned to WPs (timing/duration), and whether important risks are identified with contingency measures. Consider risks to researcher safety in adverse social/political contexts and reflect severe risks in comments/scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-criterion 3.2: Quality and capacity of the host institutions and participating organisations, including hosting arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: QUALITY AND CAPACITY OF THE HOST INSTITUTIONS AND PARTICIPATING ORGANISATIONS, INCLUDING HOSTING ARRANGEMENTS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that a Gantt Chart is included (mandatory) and is consistent and complete relative to the work plan. Assess quality of hosting arrangements, integration of researcher in team/institution, available support services, and infrastructure/facilities. For Global Fellowships consider both outgoing Third Country host and return EU MS/AC host. If a non-academic placement exists, assess its host organisation and infrastructure/capacity here. Consider associated partners' involvement if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Evaluation Report (IER) format and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The IER is the report that Evaluators draft for each allocated proposal by writing a bullet-point list of strengths and weaknesses for each sub-criteria directly in SEP. IMPORTANT: No scores are given in the IER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IER structure in SEP: 1. Excellence (strengths/weaknesses), 2. Impact (strengths/weaknesses), 3. Quality & Efficiency of Implementation (strengths/weaknesses), 2 Other Questions (scope, exceptional funding, ethics, DNSH, AI, etc.), 3 Overall comments. Evaluate as submitted (not on potential changes), do not use external websites, consider Part A and Part B and contact Vice-Chair in case of conflicting info. Keep bullet lists specific to sub-criteria. Submit IERs by deadlines; notify VC once first three IERs are in draft for feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus Report (CR) process and scoring workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapporteur drafts CR, moderates consensus discussion, suggests CR scores; Evaluators discuss and agree comments and scores; after agreement the Rapporteur submits CR for approval by the three experts; Vice-Chair performs quality check and may send CR back for revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapporteur suggests scores and notifies other experts via SEP comment box; evaluators comment until agreement; if an evaluator is unresponsive, notify VC or submit CR with tentative score. Only after the three actors approve will Vice-Chair receive 'draft ESR' for quality check. If score for criterion <5, shortcomings must be mentioned in CR. Scores should be coherent with agreed comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scale and descriptors (0–5 with decimals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores from 0 to 5 (using one decimal) for each evaluation criterion. The full range must be used with decimals (e.g. 3.3, 4.6, 4.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptor mapping: 5 = EXCELLENT (successfully addresses all relevant aspects; only minor shortcomings), 4 = VERY GOOD (addresses criterion very well; small number of shortcomings), 3 = GOOD (addresses well; number of shortcomings), 2 = FAIR (broadly addresses; significant weaknesses), 1 = POOR (inadequately addressed; serious weaknesses), 0 = FAIL (does not address or cannot be assessed due to missing/incomplete info). Overall score is weighted (Excellence 50%, Impact 30%, Implementation 20%) and automatically calculated. Ensure scores reflect the comments (strengths & weaknesses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles for evaluators (Confidentiality, Independence, Impartiality, Objectivity, Accuracy, Consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators must comply with principles: act in personal capacity and independently (public interest); treat all proposals equally and impartially; evaluate proposals as submitted and not on potential; base judgements on the three official evaluation criteria; apply same standard to all proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss evaluation matters only with fellow experts evaluating the same proposal; do not disclose names of other experts nor involvement; maintain confidentiality of documents and delete/return confidential material after work. Follow Contract Annex 1 Code of Conduct and briefing for experts on Funding & Tenders Portal. Vice-Chairs monitor quality and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest (CoI) rules for evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: You must inform REA as soon as you become aware of a CoI: before signing contract, upon receipt of proposals, or during work. A CoI exists in many defined situations (competing proposals, involvement in preparation, direct/indirect benefit, close family/personal relationships, employment/contract with applicants/subcontractors, membership of advisory groups, NCP or EEN roles, Programme Committee membership, involvement in secondment or non-academic placement, recent employment/collaboration etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a CoI is identified, decline the task. REA decides case-by-case; in limited cases REA may still invite a declared-CoI expert but exclude them from evaluating affected proposals if (e.g.) they work in a different team, departments have high autonomy, etc. REA will consider objective circumstances (employment in past three years, membership/management roles, collaborations) when deciding CoI existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments quality: DOs (how to write useful evaluation comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comments must be: relative to the proposal as it stands; specific to the relevant sub-criterion; in light of the type of action (EF or GF); clear, substantial and concise; and consistent with the score awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise, evidence-based language (e.g., 'because', 'for example'). Prefer positive qualifiers like 'very relevant, credible, very clear, precisely specified, realistic, very innovative, well formulated' etc. Explain why strengths/weaknesses exist and how they justify the score. Avoid using real names of people/institutions; use generic terms like 'host institution', 'researcher'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments quality: DON'Ts (forbidden content in evaluation comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comments must not be: a summary of the proposal; too short or too long; inappropriate, discriminatory or politically incorrect; categorical/general unverified statements; based on assumptions; or recommendations/advice on improving the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not give contradictory statements across criteria, do not penalise the same weakness under multiple criteria (no double penalisation), and do not include real names or details that might lead to factual mistakes (page numbers, amounts, years). Do not list Open Access to peer-reviewed publications as a 'strength' (it is contractual). Avoid offensive language. Use 'not clear', 'inadequate description' rather than 'missing'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal content and format requirements (Part A / Part B, page limits, fonts, margins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are composed of Part A (administrative/financial info) and Part B (scientific & training activities). Part B-1 describes Excellence, Impact and Quality & Efficiency of Implementation — maximum 10 pages for Part B-1 (excess pages invisible). Part B-2 contains CV, participating organisations, ethics/security info and letters of commitment (no page limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting: all margins at least 15 mm (excluding headers/footers). Reference fonts for body text: Times New Roman (Windows), Times/Nimbus Roman (Apple/Linux). Minimum font size 11 points (except Gantt chart and tables, min 8 points). Use standard character spacing and minimum single line spacing. Tables to illustrate only. Follow Project proposal – Technical description Part B formatting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Science practices assessment (Data Management Plan, Open Access to research data, other practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open science practices should be implemented as an integral part of the proposed methodology and assessed under Excellence (sub-criterion 1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate Research output management through a Data Management Plan as explained in the proposal; Open Access to research data (where possible); any other open science practices explained (preprints, preregistration, open peer-review, software/data sharing, citizen science involvement). If open science practices are not appropriate, check whether the proposal provides sufficient justification. Do not evaluate Open Access to peer-reviewed publications in strengths/weaknesses (contractual obligation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gantt chart requirement and consistency check
rubrics_metrics.description: A Gantt chart is mandatory and must be included in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the Gantt chart is consistent and complete in relation to the whole work plan (work packages, deliverables, milestones, secondments and placements if applicable). Inconsistencies between Gantt and work plan should be reflected as weaknesses under Implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of assessment grid and training resources
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended to use the MSCA-PF Assessment Grid to ensure all sub-criteria and additional questions are covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download the interactive assessment grid from the SEP dashboard for the relevant HORIZON-MSCA-2021-PF evaluation session. REA provides e-learning modules and exercises for experts and Vice-Chairs to support calibration and quality of reports.
